requirement: For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` has no structural obligations, so it needs no implementation roots. I reviewed the supplied roots (none) and the text of the cited requirements. `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` has no implementing edges.

Each clause describes what the agent observes:
- "MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook": the hook is the delivery channel. Any implementation that gives the session the same context at start has the same observable result. The hook's own structure is delegated to `requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`, and the text here only cites it.
- "exactly one sentence that points to the skill": this limits the content of the output, so it is observable.
- The sentence "says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill ... before starting any work": this is also message content.

The text names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface that implementations must use. Any code that produces the same context would satisfy it, however it is written. The cited `requirements.cli.setup` and `requirements.cli.overview_skill` only provide context, such as the dev-dependency condition and the skill's name. Behavior such as the message wording and the single sentence is left to the behavioral and test criteria.

behavioral: The tests cover each obligation of `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`.

**Context delivery.** The `habeas hook session-start` command runs from the project, from nested working directories, and through Symposium itself.
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start]` feeds a `SessionStart` event to the hook. It asserts that the process exits successfully and parses the response as the `SessionStart` `additionalContext` structure. That covers the nonblocking context delivery.
- `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py#def[main]` runs the real Symposium and checks that the agent output starts with the skill sentence.

**Exactly one skill sentence, with the required content.**
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_points_to_the_habeas_skill_once_setup_is_complete]` runs `habeas setup` and then asserts the whole response equals `skill_sentence_only()`. That sentence is "This project tracks requirements with Habeas; load the `habeas` skill before starting any work." The assertion covers the content (project uses Habeas, load the `habeas` skill, before any work) and that nothing else is present. It runs in both the project root and a nested directory.
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_puts_the_skill_sentence_before_the_setup_advisory]` uses a project with the dev-dependency but incomplete setup. It asserts that the context starts with the skill sentence and that `` `habeas` skill `` occurs exactly once, so the setup advisory does not add a second skill sentence. It also checks that there is a single `additionalContext`.
- The smoke test checks both the incomplete and configured states. The configured state must equal the sentence alone.

**Applicability.** The requirement gives no obligations for projects without the dev-dependency. `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_gives_no_context_outside_habeas_projects]` and `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_advises_only_when_setup_is_incomplete]` check that case anyway. Both are marked as tests of other requirements, so they are only extra evidence here.

The cited requirements `requirements.cli.setup`, `requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook` and `requirements.cli.overview_skill` are context only. The tests apply them where the subject needs them: `setup` is run to produce a configured project, and the advisory is checked in the incomplete case.

I found no untested obligation and no marking gap.

text: For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive a Symposium `SessionStart` hook. The hook MUST check whether the configuration and files required by `requirements.cli.setup`, {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.setup`, and {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.setup.configuration` are present and compatible. If not, it MUST provide nonblocking agent context saying that Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. If setup is complete or no applicable project is found, it MUST provide no setup advisory. The hook MUST NOT modify project files or run setup itself.

Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.

In a project where `habeas setup` has completed, the whole session-start agent context is one sentence such as "This project tracks requirements with Habeas; load the `habeas` skill before starting any work." {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`
